VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE

REASON: I cannot determine whether every URL listed in the repository is accessible (i.e., does not return 404) or has an archived copy in the Wayback Machine because I am not able to make network requests from this static code inspection. The repository contains URLs (in the bibliography), but there is no code or test artifacts that perform the described network checks using the Python requests library with an explicit User-Agent header, so there is no direct evidence in-repo that the test was run or passed.

EVIDENCE:
- The repository contains bibliography entries with explicit URLs at these locations (examples):
  - [repo/arxiv.bbl:14-20] contains: "URL \url{https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03553}" [/repo/arxiv.bbl:14-20].
  - [repo/arxiv.bbl:90-98] contains: "URL \url{https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948}" [/repo/arxiv.bbl:90-98].
  - [repo/arxiv.bbl:216-222] contains: "URL \url{https://maa.org/maa-invitational-competitions/}" [/repo/arxiv.bbl:216-222].
  - [repo/arxiv.bbl:306-312] contains: "URL \url{https://openreview.net/pdf?id=WE_vluYUL-X}" [/repo/arxiv.bbl:306-312].

- The repository file listing shows this is primarily a LaTeX paper and contains no Python scripts or URL-checking code (artifact): [/evidence/artifacts/file_list.txt].

- A project-wide search for terms related to performing the network checks ("requests", "User-Agent", "archive.org", "wayback", "status_code", "404") only turned up the BBL URL entries (artifact): [/evidence/artifacts/grep_results.txt].

What additional information is needed to conclude PASS or FAIL:
1) Network check results: For each URL present in repository (the four shown above and any others), a log or machine-readable output showing either:
   - an HTTP response with a non-404 status (e.g., 200) for the URL when requested with Python requests and an explicit User-Agent header; OR
   - if the URL returns 404 or is otherwise unreachable, the JSON response from the Wayback Machine Availability API (http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=example.com) showing an archived snapshot exists for that URL.

   Example of a correct check (to run locally or in CI) and the outputs I need:
   - Python snippet to run for each URL:
     import requests
     headers = {"User-Agent": "my-check-script/1.0 (+https://example.org)"}
     r = requests.get(url, headers=headers, allow_redirects=True, timeout=10)
     print(url, r.status_code)
     if r.status_code == 404:
         wa = requests.get("http://archive.org/wayback/available", params={"url": url}, headers=headers, timeout=10).json()
         print(url, "wayback:", wa)

   - Required outputs: status_code for each URL and, where status_code==404 (or request error), the Wayback API JSON showing archived snapshots (e.g., wa['archived_snapshots'] non-empty or wa['archived_snapshots'].get('closest') present).

2) Alternatively, a test run artifact (log file) produced by a script in the repo that performs those checks using requests with an explicit User-Agent and the Wayback fallback. The log must include per-URL HTTP status codes and Wayback API results for unreachable URLs.

Given the lack of network access and lack of in-repo checking code/results, I cannot confidently mark PASS or FAIL; therefore the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE.

VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE
REASON: I could not reliably verify whether the cited conference papers in the repository actually appear in the official proceedings because automated queries to an external bibliographic service (DBLP) failed with server errors (HTTP 500). Without a working external lookup I cannot obtain independent proof that each "Conference X, Year Y" citation in the main .bbl/.bib corresponds to a paper actually present in that conference's official proceedings.

EVIDENCE:
- The repository contains the generated bibliography main.bbl and a .bib file: [repo/main.bbl] and [repo/my.bib]. I inspected the .bbl to find citations that explicitly claim conference proceedings and years. Example citations from the main .bbl that state a conference and year:
  - Bourtoule et al., "Machine unlearning." cited as In 2021 IEEE symposium on security and privacy (SP), 2021. [repo/main.bbl:23-26]
  - Cao & Yang, "Towards making systems forget with machine unlearning." cited as In 2015 IEEE symposium on security and privacy, 2015. [repo/main.bbl:28-31]
  - Moosavi-Dezfooli et al., "Robustness via curvature regularization, and vice versa." cited as In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, 2019. [repo/main.bbl:212-215]

- I attempted to verify these citations by querying the DBLP public search API using Python requests with an explicit User-Agent (browser UA). That request produced an HTTP 500 error from DBLP. I saved the request log excerpt here: [/evidence/artifacts/dblp_request_log.txt]. The log shows the DBLP service returned an error page (server error), preventing automated verification.

What is needed to conclude PASS or FAIL:
- Working access to an authoritative bibliographic/proceedings source (e.g., DBLP, ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, publisher proceedings pages) from this environment so that I can confirm each cited paper is present in the official proceedings for the stated conference and year. Specifically, the DBLP search API (or an alternate reliable source) must respond successfully to queries made with an explicit User-Agent.

Given the inability to perform these external checks from this environment, the test is INCONCLUSIVE.

REASON: I cannot determine whether each URL in the repository returns a non-404 HTTP response or is archived in the Wayback Machine because I may not perform network requests in this evaluation and the repository does not contain pre-recorded results. The repo also does not include any Python code that performs these checks (no code using the requests library with an explicit User-Agent was found), so there are no in-repo artifacts showing HTTP status checks or Wayback queries.

EVIDENCE:
- URLs found in the repository:
  - State of California CCPA URL (note: contains an embedded space in the file, making it malformed as written): [repo/main.bbl:18-22] shows "Retrieved from State of California Department of Justice: https://oag. ca. gov/privacy/ccpa" (see lines 18-22 of main.bbl). The same string appears in the bibliography file: [repo/my.bib:511-516] shows the line "journal={Retrieved from State of California Department of Justice: https://oag. ca. gov/privacy/ccpa},".
  - arXiv URL: [repo/main.bbl:148-152] includes "URL \url{https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06825}." and [repo/my.bib:518-526] includes "url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06825},".

- No code in the repository that performs network checks with requests or Wayback queries:
  - There are no Python files in the repository (search returned none; repository tree contains LaTeX files, bibliography, and images). I confirmed the main source files are LaTeX: [repo/main.tex] and the pages in [repo/pages/*.tex].
  - A search for the string "requests" returned no matches in the repository (no evidence of using the Python requests library), and there are no scripts that query the Wayback Machine.

WHY THIS IS INCONCLUSIVE / WHAT I NEED TO DECIDE PASS/FAIL:
- To determine PASS or FAIL I need concrete HTTP results for each URL found in the repository (HTTP status codes for direct requests) and, if a URL returns 404, verification that the Wayback Machine has an archived copy (the JSON response from http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=...). Specifically, for each URL I need either:
  1) A successful HTTP response (status != 404) from a GET request to the URL made with an explicit User-Agent header, or
  2) The Wayback Machine availability JSON showing archived snapshots (the response body for the Wayback query indicating an archive exists).

Provide one of the following to make the verdict PASS or FAIL:
- Run logs: a simple CSV or JSON report listing each URL and the results: primary HTTP status code, and if 404 then the Wayback API JSON response (or at least a boolean indicating archive availability). The HTTP requests must be made with an explicit User-Agent header (for example, "User-Agent: repo-url-checker/1.0").
- Or grant the ability for me to execute the above network checks from this environment.

Suggested reproducible check (exact script to run locally):

python3 - <<'PY'
import requests, json
urls = [
    'https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/ccpa',
    'https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06825',
]
headers = {'User-Agent': 'repo-url-checker/1.0'}
results = {}
for u in urls:
    try:
        r = requests.get(u, headers=headers, timeout=15)
        results[u] = {'status_code': r.status_code}
        if r.status_code == 404:
            way = requests.get('http://archive.org/wayback/available', params={'url': u}, headers=headers, timeout=15)
            results[u]['wayback'] = way.json()
    except Exception as e:
        results[u] = {'error': str(e)}
print(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
PY

Notes:
- The CCPA URL in the repository contains spaces ("https://oag. ca. gov/privacy/ccpa"). Before testing the CCPA URL, normalize/remove the spaces to form the actual URL (https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/ccpa).

If you provide the run output (the JSON/CSV report) or allow network access here, I will re-evaluate and return PASS if every URL either responded without 404 or has an archived record in the Wayback Machine; otherwise I will return FAIL with evidence.

VERDICT: FAIL
REASON: Several arXiv identifiers listed in the repository's main .bib/.bbl resolve to accessible arXiv pages, but the author lists (and in one case the title formatting) on arXiv do not match the citation text included in the repository. The test requires that each listed arXiv id correspond to the paper with the same title and authors as cited; multiple entries do not meet this requirement.

EVIDENCE:
1) The repository includes arXiv entries in repo/main.bib. Example entry for arXiv ID 1802.03426 shows the cited authors in the .bib file: see [repo/main.bib:140-170]. That excerpt includes the bib entry and author field for the 1802.03426 citation.
   - Citation excerpt: [repo/main.bib:140-170]

2) The arXiv abstract page for 1802.03426 is accessible (HTTP 200) and lists an additional author (Melville) not present in the repo citation. The fetched page title and author list were recorded by the check script and stored as an artifact: [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check.txt]. The artifact shows:
   - ARXIV_URL: http://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03426
   - ARXIV_TITLE: UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction
   - ARXIV_AUTHORS: McInnes, Leland; Healy, John; Melville, James
   - BIB_AUTHOR (from repo): Leland McInnes and John Healy
   (See /evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check.txt, section for ID 1802.03426.)

3) Another example with a title/author discrepancy: the repository's .bib entry for 2307.14984 includes a LaTeX-escaped title and an author list (see [repo/main.bib:636-652]). The arXiv page for 2307.14984 is accessible and the authoritative arXiv title and author list are in the artifact. The script flagged a title mismatch and author mismatch for this ID (see /evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check.txt, section for ID 2307.14984).
   - Citation excerpt: [repo/main.bib:636-652]
   - Recorded arXiv page details: /evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check.txt (ID 2307.14984)

4) Full results collected by the checking script (includes HTTP status, arXiv page title, and arXiv authors for each found ID, and a per-ID PASS/FAIL) are saved as an artifact: [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check.txt]. The script summary reports many author mismatches and one title mismatch and concludes FINAL: FAIL.

How the evidence was gathered (verifiable):
- I extracted arXiv-style identifiers from repo/main.bib and repo/main.bbl and attempted to retrieve http://arxiv.org/abs/<id> for each, using an explicit User-Agent header. The HTTP responses and the page metadata (citation_title and citation_author meta tags when available) were recorded in /evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check.txt.
- The cited lines in the repository are shown above so anyone can independently verify the .bib/.bbl contents.

Because the test requires exact matching titles and authors, and multiple arXiv entries in the repo do not match the arXiv pages (authors differ or are shortened to "and others" in the .bib, and at least one title has formatting differences that the script flagged), the repository fails the test.

Files and locations to verify:
- repo/main.bib (contains the cited arXiv entries) — e.g. [repo/main.bib:140-170] and [repo/main.bib:636-652]
- repo/main.bbl (also contains some arXiv entries)
- /evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check.txt (recorded HTTP fetch results and comparisons)

If you want, I can re-run the checks to produce a complete per-ID diff table (showing exact quoted strings from the .bib/.bbl and the arXiv meta tags) or expand the artifact to include the full fetched HTML for each page for manual verification.

VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE
REASON: I was able to automatically check many in-proceedings citations in repo/main.bib by following the URLs provided in the bib entries. Several citations resolved to authoritative proceedings pages (ACL Anthology, PMLR, OpenReview, MLR, etc.) and the target paper pages were reachable and contain the paper (examples given below). However, multiple in-proceedings citations could not be conclusively verified because the official URLs either returned HTTP 403 (access blocked), HTTP 404 (not found at that URL), or there was no URL field in the bib entry. Because I cannot conclusively confirm presence/absence for those citations from the available evidence, the overall test outcome is INCONCLUSIVE.

EVIDENCE:
1) The repository contains the bibliography files: [/repo/main.bib] and [/repo/main.bbl]. The bib file includes many inproceedings entries; e.g. the Benedetto EMNLP 2024 entry is in main.bib lines 1-21: [/repo/main.bib:1-21]. The FAccT 'Lee' entry is at [/repo/main.bib:92-106]. The NeurIPS Salewski entry is at [/repo/main.bib:874-895]. The NeurIPS Xie entry is at [/repo/main.bib:1060-1090].

2) I performed HTTP checks (using requests with a custom User-Agent) for the inproceedings entries that include a URL in main.bib and saved the results here: [/evidence/artifacts/http_checks.json]. That file contains the status codes and final URLs the checks followed. Notable findings from that artifact (selected excerpts):

REASON: I cannot determine whether every URL is reachable (HTTP 200) or archived because I cannot perform network requests. The repository contains many external URLs (mostly in the bibliography), but it does not include any code or saved results that check URL accessibility or query the Wayback Machine using the Python requests library with an explicit User-Agent. To decide PASS/FAIL would require actually making HTTP requests (or seeing prior run logs).

EVIDENCE:
1) The repository contains many external URLs in the bibliography (examples):
   - [repo/main.bib:1-120] contains multiple Xurl entries, e.g. "https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2024.findings-emnlp.663" and "https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0020019081901113" (see that file range).
   - [repo/main.bib:240-480] contains additional Xurl entries and arXiv links such as "https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2503.19786" and "https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-emnlp.589/".
   (You can inspect the full list of URLs in repo/main.bib.)

2) The repository is a LaTeX paper; it contains only .tex/.bib/.sty/.bst files and a figs directory (no scripts that perform web checks). Listing of repository files at top level of repo:
   - repo/00README.json
   - repo/0_abstract.tex

   - repo/9.1_appendix_experiments_setup.tex
   - repo/9.2_appendix_experiments_results.tex
   - repo/9.3_appendix_proofs.tex
   - repo/9_appendix.tex
   - repo/fancyhdr.sty
   - repo/iclr2026_conference.bst
   - repo/iclr2026_conference_modified.sty
   - repo/macros.tex
   - repo/main.bbl
   - repo/main.bib
   - repo/main.tex
   - repo/math_commands.tex
   - repo/natbib.sty
   (This listing shows there are no Python scripts in the repository to perform URL / Wayback checks.)

3) There is no evidence of code that queries URLs or the Wayback Machine using Python requests with an explicit User-Agent. I searched for relevant keywords and found none (no occurrences of "requests", "wayback", "Wayback", or similar network-checking code). Example of an in-repo reference to an external URL in main.tex: [repo/main.tex:18] contains the comment: "% Optional math commands from https://github.com/goodfeli/dlbook_notation." This demonstrates external links exist in non-code files but no checking logic is present.

What I would need to convert this to PASS or FAIL:
- Either: (preferred) Run a script that (for every URL found in the repository) performs an HTTP GET with Python requests specifying an explicit User-Agent header, records whether the response is 200 (or not 404), and for any non-200/404 responses queries the Wayback Machine API (http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=...) to confirm an archived copy exists. Provide the run log / output of that script.
- Or: Provide saved results in the repository showing the accessibility status for each URL (e.g., a CSV/JSON listing url + http_status + wayback_available boolean) produced by such a script.

Because that runtime network evidence is absent, I cannot assert PASS or FAIL — therefore INCONCLUSIVE.

VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE
REASON: I could not definitively verify whether the cited conference papers actually appear in the official proceedings because online verification attempts (DBLP API queries) were blocked by the remote server (HTTP 429 Too Many Requests). Without successful web access to proceedings listings (or provided DOIs/URLs that directly prove inclusion), I cannot conclusively PASS or FAIL the test.

EVIDENCE:
1) The repository contains a main bibliography file with multiple conference citations that claim publication in named conferences and years. Representative examples from repo/main.bib:
   - [repo/main.bib:220-225] @inproceedings{vdm, ... booktitle = {Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems}, ... year = {2022} }
   - [repo/main.bib:227-232] @inproceedings{VideoComposer, ... booktitle = {Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems}, ... year = {2023} }
   - [repo/main.bib:235-240] @InProceedings{pmlr-v222-shin24a, ... booktitle = {Proceedings of the 15th Asian Conference on Machine Learning}, year = {2024} }
   - [repo/main.bib:242-247] @InProceedings{Ceylan_2023_ICCV, ... booktitle = {Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision}, year = {2023} }
   - [repo/main.bib:312-317] @InProceedings{Blattmann_2023_CVPR, ... booktitle = {Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition}, year = {2023} }
   (These citations were extracted programmatically from the same file; more entries exist — see the full bib at repo/main.bib.)

2) I attempted to verify each inproceedings entry by querying the DBLP public API (a reliable source of conference proceedings contents) using a small script. The script and its output (showing per-entry errors) were saved:
   - Script output (JSON showing attempted matches and errors): [/evidence/artifacts/check_bib_output.json]
     This file contains the parsed list of inproceedings and the error status "Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)" produced when trying to parse DBLP responses as JSON (caused by the server returning an HTML rate-limit page).

3) Direct evidence that web queries were blocked (HTTP 429) is saved here:
   - Captured DBLP response showing rate limiting for a sample query: [/evidence/artifacts/dblp_429_pix2video.txt]
     Contents begin with: "HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests" and HTML stating "You have sent too many requests in a given amount of time." This prevented successful JSON responses from DBLP and thus prevented verification.

What is needed to reach a decisive verdict (either PASS or FAIL):
- Allow the script to perform successful web requests to a reliable proceedings index (examples: DBLP, the conference's official proceedings page, IEEE Xplore/ACM Digital Library) from this environment. Specifically: remove the rate-limiting block or run the verification from an environment that can access DBLP without 429 responses. The verification script I used expects to be able to GET JSON from DBLP's search API.

Alternative ways to conclude without network access:
- Provide DOIs or direct official-proceedings URLs for each cited paper inside the .bib (e.g., add url or doi fields). If those are present in the .bib/.bbl, I could verify inclusion from the supplied metadata alone.
- Provide an offline copy of the official proceedings index (e.g., DBLP dump or conference program HTML) that I can search locally.

Summary: There is direct evidence of conference/year claims in repo/main.bib, and I attempted to verify inclusion in proceedings via DBLP. However, remote queries were blocked (HTTP 429), so verification could not complete. Therefore the correct verdict is INCONCLUSIVE until network access to proceedings pages or supporting metadata (DOIs/URLs/offline proceedings) is provided for automated verification.

(Search returned no matches in the repo.)

What is needed to reach a PASS or FAIL:
- Run-time evidence showing the HTTP status for each URL (e.g., a run log or output file) obtained by performing an HTTP GET for each URL with an explicit User-Agent header, and for any URL that returned 404, a Wayback Machine query response showing an archived snapshot exists (JSON response from http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=...).

- A short Python script that for each URL:
  1) performs requests.get(url, headers={"User-Agent": "YourAgent/1.0"}, allow_redirects=True) and records response.status_code.
  2) If status_code == 404 (or request fails), queries http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=<url> (also with the User-Agent header) and records whether an archived snapshot exists (check JSON response for "archived_snapshots" and "closest").
- Produce a results file or console log listing every URL and the outcome (OK, 404+archived, or 404+not-archived).

Because those network checks are required and not present in the repository, the correct verdict here is INCONCLUSIVE. If you can provide the runtime results (logs or the output of the suggested script), I will re-evaluate and produce a PASS or FAIL with concrete evidence extracted from those results.

Another example: entry 2107.03374 in the .bib shows the author field as "Mark Chen and Jerry Tworek and others" while the arXiv page lists the full author list; the .bib's use of "and others" is not the same author list as on arXiv.

- The .bib entry for 2107.03374 shows an incomplete author list: [/repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:134-140].

- The script's parsed arXiv metadata for 2407.16741 shows the arXiv authors starting with "Wang, Xingyao" (different from the .bib author): [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check.txt:81-87].

Additional notes:
- I ran an automated check (saved output) that requested each arXiv abs page using an explicit User-Agent and extracted title and meta authors; the full script output is saved at [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check.txt]. Some .bib titles also include braces or truncated text which caused further mismatches; the decisive failure here is the mismatch in author names for 2407.16741 (Qingyun Wang vs Xingyao Wang).

Because there exists at least one arXiv id whose cited authors do not match the arXiv page, the test fails.

REASON: All DOIs listed in the repository's main bibliography resolve via https://doi.org/<doi> to publisher landing pages, and the landing-page metadata (title and authors) matches the titles/authors given in the repository's main .bib entries. For DOIs whose publisher pages require JS to render (dl.acm.org), I fetched CrossRef citation JSON via DOI content-negotiation (application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json) to obtain canonical title/author metadata; those entries match the .bib. For Nature and IEEE DOIs I fetched the landing HTML and extracted title/author metadata. Evidence below shows the repo bibliography lines and the resolved landing-page / CrossRef metadata files.

1) DOI 10.1145/36206.36194

   - Landing page HTML includes title and authors: [ /evidence/artifacts/10.1038_s41586-023-06004-9.html:56-57 ] shows "title":"Faster sorting algorithms discovered using deep reinforcement learning" and the full author list (e.g., "Daniel J. Mankowitz", "Andrea Michi", "Anton Zhernov", ...), matching the .bib entry [repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:212-214].

   - CrossRef citation JSON (title+authors): [ /evidence/artifacts/10.1145_3620666.3651373.json:1-5 ] contains "title":"Limoncello: Prefetchers for Scale" and an author array starting with {"given":"Akanksha","family":"Jain"}, matching the .bib entry [repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:313-316].

4) DOI 10.1109/LCA.2024.3361925
   - bib entry (title + author + doi): [repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:330-339]
   - DOI resolves to: [ /evidence/artifacts/10.1109_LCA.2024.3361925.url:1-1 ] -> https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10419888/
   - Landing page HTML contains title metadata and author info: [ /evidence/artifacts/10.1109_LCA.2024.3361925.html:135-136 ] (og/twitter title) and the embedded metadata object [ /evidence/artifacts/10.1109_LCA.2024.3361925.html:365-366 ] showing "title":"R.I.P. Geomean Speedup Use Equal-Work (Or Equal-Time) Harmonic Mean Speedup Instead" and author "Lieven Eeckhout", matching the .bib entry [repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:331-334].

5) DOI 10.1145/63039.63043
   - bib entry (title + author + doi): [repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:341-352]
   - DOI resolves to: [ /evidence/artifacts/10.1145_63039.63043.url:1-1 ] -> https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/63039.63043
   - CrossRef citation JSON (title+author): [ /evidence/artifacts/10.1145_63039.63043.json:1-5 ] contains "title":"Characterizing computer performance with a single number" and author {"given":"J. E.","family":"Smith"}, matching the .bib entry [repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:341-344].

Notes on method and reliability:
- I extracted DOIs from the main bib file (repo/iclr2026_conference.bib) and used https://doi.org/<doi> to follow redirects.
- For publisher pages that render via JavaScript (ACM dl.acm.org), direct HTML fetch via curl returned a JS/Cloudflare interstitial. To get canonical bibliographic metadata I used DOI content negotiation (Accept: application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json) which returned CrossRef-hosted CSL JSON containing authoritative title and author fields for those DOIs; those JSON files are saved under /evidence/artifacts/ and cited above. CrossRef is the canonical registry for DOI metadata and is appropriate for confirming title/author matching when the publisher page requires JS.

Conclusion: Every DOI in the main .bib resolved to the expected landing page and the landing-page / CrossRef metadata matches the title and authors recorded in the repository's bibliography — therefore the test PASSes.

REASON: At least one arXiv identifier listed in the repository bibliography (arxiv.bbl) does not correspond to a paper on arXiv with the same title as cited. All looked-up arXiv pages were reachable (HTTP 200), so this is a title mismatch rather than an accessibility issue.

Notes / Methodology:
- I parsed the repository's arxiv.bbl to extract arXiv identifiers of the form yymm.nnnnn and the corresponding cited titles/authors.
- For each extracted arXiv id I performed an HTTP GET to http://arxiv.org/abs/<id> with an explicit User-Agent and read the page's citation metadata (citation_title and citation_author meta tags) to compare against the .bbl citation.
- All arXiv pages for the extracted ids returned HTTP 200, but the entry for 2406.04592 has a title that does not match the title given in the .bbl (evidence cited above), therefore the test fails.

If you want, I can produce a full CSV-style report listing every found arXiv id, the cited title/authors, the fetched arXiv title/authors, and pass/fail per entry, and save it under /evidence/artifacts/ for your review.

I could not complete those external verifications from the repository contents alone.

Specifically, the repository lacks copies or authoritative local listings of the official conference proceedings; therefore we need outbound HTTP access (or the proceedings files) to confirm presence/absence of each cited paper in the official proceedings.

I extracted the conference-style citations directly from the repository's main .bbl file. Below are representative conference citations and their locations in the file (repo/arxiv.bbl):

- Kleinberg et al. (2018). "An alternative view: When does sgd escape local minima?" In International conference on machine learning, pages 2698--2707. PMLR. [repo/arxiv.bbl:118-121]

(There are additional conference entries in the same file; the above are representative samples.)

WHAT IS NEEDED TO RESOLVE THIS TEST CASE:
- Allow this evaluation environment to perform outbound HTTP requests so I can query official proceedings pages (for example: PMLR/proceedings.mlr.press for ICML/AISTATS, NeurIPS proceedings, COLT proceedings, or the conference's official site). The test instructions permit using Python requests with an explicit User-Agent.

Or, if outbound network access is not allowed/provided:
- Provide the official proceedings pages or PDFs for each cited conference-year (e.g., ICML 2019 proceedings page or PDF) so I can check whether each cited paper appears within them.

With that external evidence I will verify each conference-year citation (searching by title and/or author) and then return a PASS if every cited paper is present in the stated official proceedings, or FAIL if any cited paper is missing, with direct citations (proceedings URLs and page numbers) as evidence.

Reason for INCONCLUSIVE: based only on repository contents I can list which citations claim conference-year publication, but I cannot irrefutably determine whether the official proceedings actually contain those papers without consulting the external proceedings sources described above.

If you enable network access to DBLP or supply the proceedings pages (or allow me to run the script against those sites), I will re-run the checks and produce a PASS (if every cited paper is found in the stated official proceedings) or FAIL (if any cited paper is not found), with direct URL evidence per citation.

import requests

]

for u in urls:

        r = requests.get(u, headers=headers, timeout=10)
        print(u, 'status', r.status_code)
        if r.status_code == 404:
            wa = requests.get('http://archive.org/wayback/available', params={'url': u}, headers=headers, timeout=10)
            print('  wayback:', wa.status_code, wa.text)

REASON: Two DOIs listed in the repository's main bibliography (reference.bib) resolve via https://doi.org/<doi> to the ACL Anthology root page (https://aclanthology.org) rather than to the specific paper landing pages. Because the test requires every listed DOI to resolve to a landing page for the specific paper cited (matching title/authors), this repository fails the test.

EVIDENCE:
1) The .bib contains the DOI entries for the two affected papers:
   - [repo/reference.bib:112-121] shows the entry for xin2020deebert including url and doi for 10.18653/v1/2020.acl-main.204:
     "url = \"https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.204/\",\n     doi = \"10.18653/v1/2020.acl-main.204\""
   - [repo/reference.bib:532-537] shows the entry for miao2021diverse including url and doi for 10.18653/v1/2020.acl-main.92:
     "url = \"https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.92/\",\n     doi = \"10.18653/v1/2020.acl-main.92\""

2) The DOI resolution results (performed with an explicit User-Agent) show these DOIs redirected to the ACL Anthology root rather than the paper pages:
   - [/evidence/artifacts/doi_check_results.json:10-15] (entry for 10.18653/v1/2020.acl-main.204):
     { "req_url": "https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2020.acl-main.204", "status": 200, "final_url": "https://aclanthology.org", "title_tag": "ACL Anthology" }
   - [/evidence/artifacts/doi_check_results.json:16-22] (entry for 10.18653/v1/2020.acl-main.92):
     { "req_url": "https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2020.acl-main.92", "status": 200, "final_url": "https://aclanthology.org", "title_tag": "ACL Anthology" }

3) For contrast, other DOIs in the same .bib resolved to specific paper pages (showing the checker worked and that the problem is specific to some DOIs):
   - [/evidence/artifacts/doi_check_results.json:24-29] (10.18653/v1/2021.naacl-main.168) final_url: "https://aclanthology.org/2021.naacl-main.168/" with title_tag matching the paper.
   - [/evidence/artifacts/doi_check_results.json:66-70] (10.48550/arXiv.2502.13842) final_url: "https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13842" with title_tag matching the paper.

Notes on methodology and reproducibility:
- I extracted DOIs from repo/reference.bib and resolved each with HTTP GET to https://doi.org/<doi> using a script that sets User-Agent "Repo-DOI-Checker/1.0 (+https://doi.org)". The raw per-DOI resolution output was saved to /evidence/artifacts/doi_check_results.json and a subsequent verification summary to /evidence/artifacts/doi_verification3.json (these files contain the full fetch results and basic title/author checks).
- Because at least one DOI did not redirect to the specific paper landing page required by the test (they redirected to the publisher root), the test condition "Every listed DOI must resolve ... to a landing page for the specific paper cited" is not satisfied.

If you want, I can:
- Try re-checking with different HTTP headers or follow-up requests to see whether the publisher blocks DOI redirects for certain clients.
- Attempt to fetch the expected paper pages directly (the URLs shown in reference.bib's url fields) and compare titles/authors as a secondary check.

- /evidence/artifacts/doi_verification3.json
- /evidence/artifacts/doi_verification2.json
- /evidence/artifacts/doi_summary.json

VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE
REASON: The repository's main bibliography (repo/reference.bib) contains multiple citations that claim publication in specific conference proceedings (for example NeurIPS 2025), but many of those entries only point to OpenReview (or lack any proceedings URL/DOI). VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE
REASON: I could not deterministically verify for all citations that a paper claimed to be published in “Conference X, Year Y” actually appears in the official proceedings for that conference/year. The repository’s main bibliography (arxiv.bib) contains many inproceedings entries that list only title, booktitle (conference abbreviation) and year but do not include DOIs or unambiguous persistent identifiers. I attempted to verify entries automatically using the CrossRef API (HTTP requests with an explicit User-Agent) but the API responses are ambiguous for many titles (common phrases, truncated/braced titles, or multiple unrelated matches). Because the bib entries lack DOIs and automated title searches returned many unrelated candidate records, I cannot confidently conclude PASS or FAIL for the repository as a whole without further authoritative data or manual checks.

EVIDENCE:
- The repository main bibliography file containing the citations I inspected: [/workdir/repo/arxiv.bib:10-20] (example entry Ajay2023DecisionDiffuser: booktitle = ICLR, year = 2023) and [/workdir/repo/arxiv.bib:22-36] (example entry Andrychowicz2017: booktitle = NeurIPS, year = 2017). The full bibliography file is at [/workdir/repo/arxiv.bib].
- I saved the CrossRef search results I obtained (showing multiple ambiguous/unrelated candidate matches for many titles) to [/evidence/artifacts/crossref_matches.json]. This file contains the raw matched items returned by the CrossRef API for each bib entry I tried to check; it demonstrates the ambiguity (e.g., many matches with unrelated container titles or differing years).

What additional information is needed to reach a conclusive verdict (exactly):
1) DOIs (or other persistent identifiers) for the inproceedings entries in the main .bib/.bbl so each cited paper can be looked up unambiguously and the container/title and publication year validated against the official proceedings metadata (CrossRef/DOI resolution or publisher pages).
2) OR permission to perform manual checks against the official proceedings pages (publisher/ACM/IEEE/Springer/dblp pages) for each conference-year and the exact mapping from the bib’s booktitle abbreviations (e.g., “NeurIPS”, “ICLR”, “ICML”) to the official proceedings URLs. Manual inspection of the publisher proceedings TOC pages (or a reliable index like DBLP with a clear mapping) is required for authoritative verification.

Because neither unambiguous identifiers are present nor did automated title searches yield reliable confirmations for all items, the correct outcome under the testing rubric is INCONCLUSIVE.

EVIDENCE:
- The URL appears in the repository source file [/workdir/repo/arxiv.tex:4-4] (line 4):
  - [/workdir/repo/arxiv.tex:4-4] shows the line: "% Optional math commands from https://github.com/goodfeli/dlbook_notation." (the trailing dot is part of the literal text in the file).

- The URL-checking code used an explicit User-Agent and performed HTTP requests with requests.get (evidence that the test used Python requests and set a UA):
  - [/workdir/repo/check_urls.py:42-50] sets UA = 'repo-url-checker/1.0 (+https://example.com)' and calls requests.get(url, headers={'User-Agent': UA}, ...).

- The run results (JSON) produced by the check are saved under /evidence/artifacts/results.json and include the failing URL with http_status 404 and wayback: false:
  - [/evidence/artifacts/results.json:1-80] contains the entry:
    {
      "url": "https://github.com/goodfeli/dlbook_notation.",
      "occurrences": ["/workdir/repo/arxiv.tex"],
      "status": "404",
      "http_status": 404,
      "error": null,
      "wayback": false
    }

Because the test requires every URL to either be accessible without a 404 or to exist in the Wayback Machine, and the exact URL string found in the repository returns 404 and has no Wayback snapshot, the repository FAILs the test.

Notes:
- The failing URL includes a trailing dot in the source file. If the intended URL was without the dot (https://github.com/goodfeli/dlbook_notation), that corrected URL may behave differently; however the test is applied to the literal URLs present in the repository files. If you want the check to treat trailing punctuation as not part of the URL, rerun the check with URL-normalization rules and re-evaluate.

Key mismatch examples (excerpted from the artifact):
  - 2412.19437 (arXiv page metadata): arxiv_authors = "DeepSeek-AI; Liu, Aixin; Feng, Bei; ..." and arxiv_title = "DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report". See [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check_filtered.json] (entry for 2412.19437). The repository reference author field is "{DeepSeek-AI}" (see [/repo/references.bib:258-260]). The comparison in /evidence/artifacts/arxiv_compare.json shows title_match: true, author_match: false for 2412.19437, i.e. authors do not match exactly. See [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_compare.json] (entry "2412.19437").
  - 2501.12948 (arXiv page metadata): arxiv_authors lists many named authors (DeepSeek team + individuals); repo reference author = {{DeepSeek-AI}}. Comparison shows author_match: false. See [/repo/references.bib:269-276] and [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check_filtered.json] and [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_compare.json] (entry "2501.12948").
  - 2503.19786 (arXiv page metadata): arxiv_authors is the set of authors shown on arXiv; repo reference author = {Google, Gemma Team}. The compare artifact shows author_match: false. See [/repo/references.bib:183-191] and [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check_filtered.json] and [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_compare.json] (entry "2503.19786").
  - 2507.06261 (arXiv page metadata): arxiv_authors lists named authors on arXiv; repo reference author = {Google, Gemini Team}. The compare artifact shows author_match: false. See [/repo/references.bib:280-288] and [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check_filtered.json] and [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_compare.json] (entry "2507.06261").

- For completeness: the set of arXiv identifiers considered (extracted from arXiv-related fields in the main .bib/.bbl) was:
  2306.11932, 2307.15217, 2310.11564, 2312.14925, 2410.12971, 2411.15594, 2412.16746, 2412.19437, 2501.01031, 2501.12948, 2503.15484, 2503.19786, 2507.05187, 2507.06261
  These IDs and the HTTP 200 status for their arXiv pages are recorded in [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_check_filtered.json].

- The automated comparison between the repository's expected titles/authors and the arXiv page metadata is stored in [/evidence/artifacts/arxiv_compare.json]; that file shows which IDs matched both title and authors and which did not. In particular, 2412.19437, 2501.12948, 2503.19786 and 2507.06261 are marked with author_match:false.

Conclusion: Because at least these arXiv entries in the main bibliography do not have matching authors on the corresponding arXiv pages (even though the pages are reachable), the test condition ("paper with the same title and authors as cited") is not satisfied for every listed arXiv id. Therefore the test fails.

- Re-run a more conservative author/title matching (e.g. match organization names or first author only) if you prefer a different matching policy.

Re-run the provided script/configured checks (or allow me to re-run them here). Recommended: ensure network egress to port 443 is allowed and increase timeouts if needed.

If you enable network access or provide the requested HTTP responses, I will: re-run the resolution for each DOI, collect final landing URLs and page titles/author metadata, and compare them against the titles/authors listed in the .bib/.bbl to produce a PASS/FAIL verdict with per-DOI evidence.

VERDICT: PASS
REASON: I examined the paper's main bibliography (repo/main.bbl) and verified that every citation that explicitly claims publication in a conference proceedings ("Proceedings of ...", conference name + year) corresponds to an entry in that conference's official proceedings. Verification was done by checking the bibliography lines and programmatically resolving the bibliography URLs/DOIs (or searching the official proceedings index) using requests with an explicit User-Agent; Crossref / proceedings indices were consulted where direct publisher pages returned access-restricted (403) responses. All such citations in main.bbl were found in the official proceedings.

EVIDENCE:
- The main bibliography contains conference publication claims; examples:
  - ACL 2024 entry with DOI and ACL Anthology URL: [repo/main.bbl:8-13]
  - FAccT 2024 entry with ACM DOI: [repo/main.bbl:58-64]
  - ICML (v235) position paper present in ICML proceedings: [repo/main.bbl:288-292]
  - Another ACL 2024 entry with ACL Anthology URL: [repo/main.bbl:300-305]

- Machine-verifiable verification results (programmatic checks of URLs/DOIs and proceedings indices) are saved here: /evidence/artifacts/verification_results.json. This file lists each checked bibliography entry, the URL/DOI used, whether it was verified, and the verification evidence (HTTP status, Crossref metadata, or proceedings index match). Cite: [/evidence/artifacts/verification_results.json]

Notes on methodology (so evidence can be independently reproduced):
- I parsed repo/main.bbl to find entries containing "Proceedings". For each entry I attempted:
  1) Fetch the provided URL (if present) with requests and a custom User-Agent.
  2) If a DOI was present (or URL pointed to a DOI), I queried Crossref (https://api.crossref.org/works/{doi}) to obtain container-title/publisher metadata.
  3) For ICML entries without an explicit URL/DOI in the .bbl I searched the official ICML proceedings index (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/) for the paper title/authors.
- Where direct publisher pages returned HTTP 403 (e.g. dl.acm.org or doi.org redirects for some ACM/PNAS pages), Crossref returned metadata confirming the paper is in the expected proceedings; that Crossref metadata is included in the saved verification_results.json.

Given the direct evidence in the bibliography and the corroborating checks (publisher pages that returned 200, Crossref metadata, or proceedings index matches), the repository PASSes the test.

VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE

REASON: The repository contains many external URLs (in the bibliography and LaTeX files), but there is no code or test artifact in the repo that actually performs HTTP requests or queries the Wayback Machine to verify their accessibility. I cannot perform network requests from this analysis to check HTTP status codes or query the Wayback API. Therefore I cannot determine whether every URL is accessible (non-404) or archived in the Wayback Machine.

EVIDENCE:
- The repository’s bibliography and LaTeX output include many external URLs which would need to be checked. Representative files containing those URLs include:
  - [repo/main.bbl:1-260] (contains many URL entries such as https://aclanthology.org/2024.acl-long.671/, https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-3-7-sonnet, http://arxiv.org/abs/2307.15217, https://deepmind.google/models/gemini/pro/, https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-1/, etc.)
  - [repo/references.bib:1-220] (contains many url fields, e.g. https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1530/, https://x.ai/news/grok-4, https://deepmind.google/models/gemini/pro/, https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-1/, http://arxiv.org/abs/2306.11932, and many others).

- There is no code in the repository that performs the described checks or that demonstrates setting an explicit User-Agent when using the requests library. (I searched the repository for common indicators such as usage of the 'requests' library and for references to 'wayback' or 'archive.org' and found no occurrences.)

What is needed to make a conclusive determination:
1) Either run a URL-checking script (not present in the repo) that, for every URL found in the repository, performs an HTTP GET and records the status code and/or queries the Wayback Machine API at http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=<url> when a 404 is returned. The script should use the Python requests library and include an explicit User-Agent header (for example: headers={'User-Agent': 'repo-url-checker/1.0'}).

Suggested command to produce the needed evidence (to be run in an environment with outbound network access):
- Python example (outline):
  - Parse URLs from repo/references.bib and repo/main.bbl.
  - For each URL:
    - Send requests.get(url, allow_redirects=True, timeout=10, headers={'User-Agent':'repo-url-checker/1.0'}) and record status_code.
    - If status_code == 404 or request fails, query Wayback: requests.get('http://archive.org/wayback/available', params={'url':url}, headers={'User-Agent':'repo-url-checker/1.0'}) and record the JSON response indicating archived availability.
  - Produce a report listing each URL and whether it was reachable (non-404) or had a Wayback archive.

2) Provide the run output (report/log) from that script showing per-URL status codes and Wayback responses, or else provide the raw HTTP responses for verification.

Because the repository itself does not include such a script or recorded results and I cannot perform network access here, the correct verdict is INCONCLUSIVE.

REASON: The repository's main .bbl contains at least one arXiv identifier whose arXiv page lists different authors than the citation in the .bbl. Kingma and Max Welling, so the authors do not match the citation.

EVIDENCE:
- Citation in repository showing the entry and arXiv identifier: [repo/_main.bbl:102-105]
  - Lines (excerpt):
    102	\bibitem[Kingma(2013)]{kingma2013auto}
    103	Diederik~P Kingma.
    104	\newblock Auto-encoding variational bayes.
    105	\newblock \emph{arXiv preprint arXiv:1312.6114}, 2013.
- arXiv page for that identifier (accessed with an explicit User-Agent) shows a different author list:
  - URL: http://arxiv.org/abs/1312.6114
  - Parsed title from the arXiv page: "Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes"
  - Parsed authors from the arXiv page: "Diederik P Kingma, Max Welling"
  - Evidence from the check script run in the environment (excerpt):
    - For 1312.6114: http_ok True
      cited_authors: Diederik~P Kingma.
      cited_title: Auto-encoding variational bayes
      page_title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
      page_authors: Diederik P Kingma, Max Welling

Because at least one arXiv entry fails the "same title and authors as cited" condition, the overall test fails.

Notes:
- All arXiv identifiers found in repo/_main.bbl were fetched; the automated check reported HTTP 200 for each. The single mismatch above is sufficient to produce a FAIL verdict. If you want, I can produce a full CSV listing all identifiers with the citation vs arXiv title/authors for review.

VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE
REASON: I could not reliably verify whether the cited conference papers actually appear in the official proceedings because external verification attempts (DBLP API) returned server errors / non-JSON pages from the queried service. Without successful access to authoritative proceedings pages (e.g. conference proceedings on openaccess.thecvf.com for CVPR/ICCV, ACM Digital Library for ACM-MM, Springer/LNCS for ECCV) or another reliable index, I cannot confirm or refute the TEST_CASE.

EVIDENCE:
- The repository's main bibliography is _main.bbl and contains multiple citations that explicitly claim publication in conference proceedings (examples below). These are the citations that require verification that the official proceedings for the stated conference/year include the paper:
  - [repo/_main.bbl:62-66] Guo et al., "Action2motion: Conditioned generation of 3d human motions." In Proceedings of the 28th ACM International Conference on Multimedia, 2020.
  - [repo/_main.bbl:67-71] Guo et al., "Generating diverse and natural 3d human motions from text." In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 2022.
  - [repo/_main.bbl:111-115] Kolotouros et al., "Learning to Reconstruct 3D Human Pose and Shape via Model-Fitting in the Loop." In 2019 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), 2019.
  - [repo/_main.bbl:121-124] Li and Dai, "Genzi: Zero-shot 3d human-scene interaction generation." In Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, 2024.
  - [repo/_main.bbl:188-191] Pishchulin et al., "Deepcut: ..." In Proceedings of the IEEE conference on computer vision and pattern recognition, 2016.
  - [repo/_main.bbl:254-257] Von Marcard et al., "Recovering accurate 3d human pose ..." In Proceedings of the European conference on computer vision (ECCV), 2018.
  - [repo/_main.bbl:269-273] Xu et al., "GHUM & GHUML: ..." In 2020 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 2020.
  (All above citations appear in repo/_main.bbl; see those line ranges.)

- I attempted automated verification by querying the DBLP public API for these titles and saved the raw responses under /evidence/artifacts. The DBLP requests returned an HTML error page (500) rather than JSON, preventing reliable automated confirmation. Example saved responses (created during the attempt):
  - /evidence/artifacts/dblp_conf_items.json (the list of conference items extracted from _main.bbl)
  - /evidence/artifacts/dblp_raw/result_2.txt (raw HTTP response for one DBLP query showing an HTML error/500 page)

Why this is INCONCLUSIVE and what is needed to reach PASS/FAIL:
- To PASS or FAIL the test we must confirm for each citation in repo/_main.bbl that claims publication in a specific conference and year whether the paper appears in the official proceedings of that conference for that year.
- I could not complete those checks because the external index I tried (DBLP) returned error pages. To complete the verification, one of the following is required:
  1) Network access that allows successful HTTP requests to authoritative proceedings hosts (examples):
     - CVPR/ICCV papers: https://openaccess.thecvf.com (per-year proceedings and paper pages)
     - ACM Multimedia / ACM DL: https://dl.acm.org
     - ECCV (Springer LNCS): https://link.springer.com (or an official ECCV proceedings page)
     - DBLP: https://dblp.org (if the API responds successfully)
     The verifier should use a custom User-Agent (as I attempted) and retrieve either the proceedings index page for the conference/year or the DBLP record for the paper and confirm the venue and year.
  2) Alternatively, provide the official proceedings files (HTML or PDF index or TOC) for the relevant conferences/years checked locally in the repository, so I can match titles/authors directly without external web access.

If you want, I can re-run the automated checks (using the saved list of conference citations) against specific proceedings hosts (openaccess.thecvf.com, dl.acm.org, link.springer.com) now — but I will need working network access to those services from this environment (or you can provide the proceedings pages/PDFs).

REASON: The repository's main bibliography (main.bbl) contains several citations that explicitly claim publication in conference proceedings (ICLR and NeurIPS). I attempted to verify presence of those papers in the official proceedings by running automated web searches (using a requests-based script that queries DuckDuckGo HTML and looks for links to official proceedings domains), but the automated search did not return verifiable proceedings links for any of the conference-cited papers. Because the script was unable to locate definitive links to the official proceedings pages, I cannot conclusively determine whether those cited papers actually appear in the stated conference proceedings.

EVIDENCE:
- Conference-cited entries in the repository main bibliography (asserting publication in conference proceedings):
  - Dziri et al., "Faith and fate: Limits of transformers on compositionality." [/repo/main.bbl:18-21]
  - Lee et al., "Teaching arithmetic to small transformers." [/repo/main.bbl:54-57]
  - Liu et al., "Towards understanding grokking: An effective theory of representation learning." [/repo/main.bbl:64-67]
  - Muennighoff et al., "Scaling data-constrained language models." [/repo/main.bbl:74-77]
  - Okawa et al., "Compositional abilities emerge multiplicatively: Exploring diffusion models on a synthetic task." [/repo/main.bbl:89-92]
  - Schaeffer et al., "Are emergent abilities of large language models a mirage?" [/repo/main.bbl:104-107]

- Automated search log (script output showing no candidate proceeding links were found in the HTML search results): [/evidence/artifacts/search_log.txt]

What is needed to reach a PASS/FAIL decision:
- Direct checks of the official proceedings pages for the specified conferences/years (ICLR 2024 and the relevant NeurIPS volumes/years). For example:
  - ICLR official accepted-papers listing on OpenReview (https://openreview.net) for ICLR 2024.
  - NeurIPS proceedings index pages for the years quoted (the repository lists "Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems" with volume numbers and years). Typical official domains include proceedings.neurips.cc, papers.nips.cc, and neurips.cc.

If you want, I can (A) try another automated lookup strategy (e.g., query multiple search engines or directly crawl likely proceedings indexes), or (B) you can grant/confirm internet access or provide the proceedings URLs (or DOIs) to check directly. The exact URLs (or DOIs) for the official proceedings pages are required to conclusively PASS or FAIL this test.

(See file and line ranges for verification.)
- The rendered bibliography also contains a URL reference to nanoGPT: [/repo/main.bbl:43-47].
- The paper checklist includes links to NeurIPS guidance pages: [/repo/sec/checklist.tex:105-107] (CodeSubmissionPolicy), [/repo/sec/checklist.tex:156-157] (EthicsGuidelines). Another NeurIPS URL appears at [/repo/sec/checklist.tex:252].
- There is a commented arXiv link in the archive notes: [/repo/archive/ideas.tex:42] contains "%https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.08819".

These file citations are present in the repository and sufficient to show which external URLs would need to be validated, but they do not contain any validation logic or recorded validation results.

WHAT IS NEEDED TO DECIDE PASS/FAIL (exactly):
To determine PASS vs FAIL you (or a CI job) must run network checks. Exactly one of the following must be provided and its output included in the repository (or provided to me) to change the verdict to PASS or FAIL:

1) A validation report (file) listing each URL and the result of checking it:
   - For each URL: HTTP status code from a GET request using Python requests with an explicit User-Agent header (e.g. headers={"User-Agent": "repo-url-checker/1.0 (+mailto:you@example.com)"}).
   - If the response status is 404 (or another error), include the JSON response from the Wayback Machine availability API: GET "http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=<URL>" (also with an explicit User-Agent). Record whether archiveSnapshots.available == true and include the archived snapshot URL(s).
   - The report should be machine- and human-readable (e.g. JSON or CSV) and saved to the repo (e.g. /repo/url_validation/report.json) or attached.

OR

2) A script in the repository that performs the checks above and can be run in CI, plus instructions. For example, a Python script that:
   - Extracts URLs from known files (e.g., bib.bib, main.bbl, .tex files)
   - For each URL does requests.get(url, headers={"User-Agent": "repo-url-checker/1.0"})
   - If response.status_code == 404: queries Wayback API at "http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=<url>" with same User-Agent and records the JSON output
   - Writes a report file with URL, status_code, and wayback info

If you provide either (1) or (2) and the report shows that every URL either returned a non-404 HTTP status OR has a Wayback snapshot, I will change the verdict to PASS and include the report as evidence. If any URL returns 404 and has no Wayback snapshot, I will change the verdict to FAIL and cite the failing URL(s) and their checks.

EXAMPLE CHECKER (run locally / in CI):

Save as repo/scripts/check_urls.py and run with Python 3.8+.


(Example script omitted from this message to keep output concise—if you want, I will produce the exact script and instructions.)

SUMMARY: Repository contains external URLs but no network-checking code or recorded results. Because network checking is required and I cannot perform web requests here, the test is INCONCLUSIVE. Provide a validation report or a script + results and I will re-evaluate to PASS or FAIL.

VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE
REASON: The repository contains a small set of external URLs, but I cannot perform live HTTP requests or query the Wayback Machine from this environment. The test requires confirming that each URL returns a non-404 response or has an archived copy, which needs network access and actual HTTP responses. That information is not available from static code inspection alone.

EVIDENCE:
- The repository contains the following URLs that need to be checked (found in the listed files):
  - https://github.com/goodfeli/dlbook_notation — referenced in a comment: [/repo/iclr2026.tex:5-5]
  - https://github.com/Quantumcraft616/COLER — paper claims code is available at this URL: [/repo/iclr2026.tex:81-81]
  - https://github.com/facebookresearch/detectron2 — cited in the bibliography: [/repo/iclr2026.bib:183-184]
  - https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.16319 — cited in the bibliography: [/repo/iclr2026.bib:364-364]

Why this is INCONCLUSIVE and what I need to conclude PASS or FAIL:
- To mark PASS I would need verifiable HTTP responses showing each URL is accessible (status != 404) OR evidence from the Wayback Machine API that an archived copy exists for any URL that returns 404. Specifically, for each URL above I need either:
  1) The HTTP status code for a GET (or HEAD) request to the exact URL (preferably with a short response snippet), showing it is not 404; OR
  2) If the GET returns 404, the JSON response from the Wayback Machine availability API for the host (e.g. http://archive.org/wayback/available?url=example.com) showing an archived snapshot exists.
- The test also requires confirming that web requests may be made using the Python requests library with an explicit User-Agent header. I cannot probe the network here to demonstrate that such requests succeed; I need either:
  - The ability to run the following Python script in an environment with outbound HTTP access, or
  - Logged output (HTTP status codes and Wayback API JSON) produced by running the script below in such an environment.

Reproducible script to run (copy-paste into a Python environment with internet access):

import requests

USER_AGENT = 'repo-url-checker/1.0 (+https://example.com)'
HEADERS = {'User-Agent': USER_AGENT}

urls = [
    'https://github.com/goodfeli/dlbook_notation',
    'https://github.com/Quantumcraft616/COLER',
    'https://github.com/facebookresearch/detectron2',
    'https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.16319',
]

wayback_api = 'http://archive.org/wayback/available?url={domain}'

results = {}
for url in urls:
    try:
        r = requests.get(url, headers=HEADERS, timeout=15)
        results[url] = {'status': r.status_code, 'reason': r.reason}
    except Exception as e:
        # on exception, record and query Wayback
        results[url] = {'error': str(e)}
        # query wayback for the domain
        import urllib.parse
        domain = urllib.parse.urlparse(url).netloc
        try:
            w = requests.get(wayback_api.format(domain=domain), headers=HEADERS, timeout=10)
            results[url]['wayback'] = w.json()
        except Exception as we:
            results[url]['wayback_error'] = str(we)

import json
print(json.dumps(results, indent=2))

What I will accept as final evidence to change the verdict to PASS or FAIL:
- For PASS: For every URL in the Evidence list above, either a recorded HTTP status != 404 returned by the script above, or a Wayback Machine JSON showing an archived snapshot exists. The printed JSON or a log file containing the same information is sufficient.
- For FAIL: For any URL, a recorded HTTP 404 response and the Wayback Machine response showing no archived snapshot for that domain.

Summary of static findings (already shown in Evidence): The repository references 4 external URLs that must be checked; their locations are cited above. No code in the repository performs HTTP requests or Wayback queries (I searched for usage of the requests library and found none), so live checks are required to determine accessibility.

If you want, I can (A) provide a standalone script file saved into the repo (e.g. /evidence/artifacts/check_urls.py) for you to run and then paste the output here, or (B) if you can run the script above and provide the results, I will convert those into a PASS/FAIL verdict with cited evidence. Please indicate which you prefer.

VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE
REASON: The repository's main bibliography is the file /workdir/repo/iclr2026_conference.bbl and it contains multiple citations that claim publication in specific conferences and years (e.g., ICLR 2024/2025, ICML 2025, NeurIPS 2021/2022, EMNLP 2018). I attempted to verify those claims using the CrossRef API (queried with an explicit User-Agent). CrossRef returned a clear match for the EMNLP 2018 paper (HotpotQA), but for multiple other conference-cited papers there were no clear matches in the top CrossRef results. Because CrossRef coverage and title variations can be incomplete, absence from CrossRef is not definitive evidence the paper is not in the official proceedings. To make a conclusive PASS or FAIL I need direct evidence from the official proceedings pages for each conference-year pairing (ICLR/OpenReview proceedings for ICLR years, PMLR for ICML proceedings, proceedings.neurips.cc for NeurIPS, ACL Anthology for EMNLP, etc.) or authoritative metadata (DOI/Proceedings listing) that shows the specific paper is (or is not) present in those proceedings.

Specifically, additional information required to conclude PASS or FAIL:
- Programmatic access (or manual links) to the official proceedings pages for each conference-year mentioned in the .bbl, so I can match the exact paper title + authors to the proceedings entry. Examples:
  - ICLR 2024 proceedings (OpenReview / ICLR.cc group page listing accepted papers)
  - ICLR 2025 proceedings
  - ICML 2025 proceedings (PMLR volume listing)
  - NeurIPS proceedings for 2021 and 2022 (proceedings.neurips.cc)
  - ACL Anthology entries for EMNLP 2018 (already matched via CrossRef)
- Alternatively, authoritative metadata (DOI or direct proceedings URLs) for each cited conference paper.

Because I cannot reliably determine presence/absence in the official proceedings for several cited papers with the information available, the result is INCONCLUSIVE.

EVIDENCE:
- Main bibliography containing the conference claims: [/workdir/repo/iclr2026_conference.bbl:28-36] (example ICLR 2024 entry: "Large language models cannot self-correct reasoning yet. In International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), 2024.")
- Additional conference-cited entries in the same .bbl: [/workdir/repo/iclr2026_conference.bbl:58-66] (ICLR 2025), [/workdir/repo/iclr2026_conference.bbl:64-66] (ICML 2025), [/workdir/repo/iclr2026_conference.bbl:70-72] (ICLR 2019), [/workdir/repo/iclr2026_conference.bbl:92-96] (NeurIPS 2022), [/workdir/repo/iclr2026_conference.bbl:98-101] (EMNLP 2018), [/workdir/repo/iclr2026_conference.bbl:112-116] (ICML 2025), [/workdir/repo/iclr2026_conference.bbl:118-121] (ICML 2025).
- Partial CrossRef verification results saved as an artifact: [/evidence/artifacts/crossref_results.txt]. This shows a clear CrossRef match for the EMNLP 2018 HotpotQA paper, and notes that other conference-cited titles did not produce clear CrossRef matches in the top results (so further verification against the official proceedings is required).

If you want, I can now:
- Run targeted checks against each conference's official proceedings website (OpenReview for ICLR, PMLR for ICML, proceedings.neurips.cc for NeurIPS, ACL Anthology for EMNLP) and produce per-paper pass/fail evidence (screenshots/HTML snippets or direct proceedings URLs). I will use an explicit User-Agent for web requests. Or,
- You can provide proceedings URLs/DOIs for the relevant conference-year and I will match them to the .bbl entries and produce a PASS/FAIL verdict.

REASON: One of the arXiv identifiers listed in the repository points to an arXiv page whose title does not match the title recorded in the repository bibliography. Specifically, the repo cites arXiv:2502.02748 with the title "ReGNet: Reciprocal Space-Aware Long-Range Modeling and Multi-Property Prediction for Crystals" but the arXiv abstract page at http://arxiv.org/abs/2502.02748 has the title "ReciNet: Reciprocal Space-Aware Long-Range Modeling for Crystalline Property Prediction" (authors match). This is a direct mismatch of the paper title for that identifier, so the test fails.

EVIDENCE:
- The repository .bib entry showing the cited title and arXiv id: [/repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:106-110] (shows title "ReGNet: Reciprocal Space-Aware Long-Range Modeling and Multi-Property Prediction for Crystals" and journal entry with arXiv id 2502.02748).

Additional context (for completeness):
- Other arXiv IDs found in the main .bib/.bbl were checked and their pages were reachable (HTTP 200) and authors match the bibliography entries. See the automated summary for all IDs: [/evidence/artifacts/results.txt:1-5].

Because the test requires that every listed arXiv id corresponds to an arXiv page for the paper with the same title and authors as cited, the mismatch for arXiv:2502.02748 causes the overall test to FAIL.

VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE
REASON: The repository contains bibliography entries that claim specific conference+year publications (e.g. ICLR 2025 and CVPR 2021), but I cannot verify whether the official proceedings for those conferences and years contain the cited papers because my environment could not reach external websites (DBLP / conference proceedings / IEEE Xplore / ICLR proceedings). External verification via web queries is required to determine PASS/FAIL and those queries failed from this environment.

EVIDENCE:
- The .bbl contains entries that explicitly cite conference name and year (examples):
  - Ito et al., "Rethinking the role of frames for se (3)-invariant crystal structure modeling." In The Thirteenth International Conference on Learning Representations, 2025. [repo/iclr2026_conference.bbl:110-114]
  - Meyer, "An alternative probabilistic interpretation of the huber loss." In Proceedings of the ieee/cvf conference on computer vision and pattern recognition, pp. 5261--5269, 2021. [repo/iclr2026_conference.bbl:160-164]

- The corresponding .bib entries that claim these conference+year publications are present:
  - [repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:316-321] (@inproceedings{ito2025rethinking, ... booktitle={The Thirteenth International Conference on Learning Representations}, year={2025})
  - [repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:352-358] (@inproceedings{meyer2021alternative, ... booktitle={Proceedings of the ieee/cvf conference on computer vision and pattern recognition}, pages={5261--5269}, year={2021})

Because the test requires checking the official proceedings for Conference X in Year Y to confirm the paper is present, I need live access to bibliographic/proceedings sources. To complete the check I need one of the following exact verifications done (these are the precise actions to perform):

1) Query DBLP or similar bibliographic index for each paper title and confirm a record where venue matches the conference name (ICLR or CVPR) and year equals the cited year. Example API call:
   - GET "https://dblp.org/search/publ/api?q=<URL-encoded title>&format=json" with header "User-Agent: repo-checker/1.0". Verify returned record has "venue" containing the conference name and "year" equal to the cited year.

2) Or retrieve the official proceedings / table-of-contents page for the conference/year and confirm the paper title and authors appear in the TOC. For example:
   - CVPR 2021 proceedings page (IEEE/CVF): fetch the CVPR 2021 proceedings TOC and search for the title "An alternative probabilistic interpretation of the huber loss" or the author "Gregory P Meyer".
   - ICLR 2025 proceedings page (ICLR/OpenReview/ICLR.cc): fetch ICLR 2025 accepted papers list / proceedings and search for the Ito paper title and authors.

If you can run these web requests from an environment with outbound network access, return the responses (or the URLs/HTML snippets showing the matching TOC entries) and I will re-evaluate. With those verifications I can produce a PASS (if all cited conference-year entries are found in the official proceedings) or FAIL (if any cited conference-year entry is missing).

Summary of what I checked locally:
- Scanned the main bibliography files in the repo (/repo/iclr2026_conference.bib and /repo/iclr2026_conference.bbl) and extracted the citations that explicitly state a conference venue and year. Those are cited above with file/line references. External verification failed because outbound HTTP requests from this environment returned errors, so I cannot conclude PASS or FAIL.

   4) Confirmation from the repository owner that the DOI-to-URL mapping is correct (e.g., author-provided publisher URLs) and that the landing page title/authors match the listed reference.

VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE
REASON: I cannot fully determine whether every paper that is cited as published in a given conference/year is actually present in that conference's official proceedings because several conference-type citations in the repository’s main .bib do not contain an explicit DOI or proceedings URL. Those entries therefore require checking external proceedings pages (publisher/anthology/openreview/etc.) to confirm presence. I do not have (from the repository alone) the definitive evidence of presence/absence for those citations.

EVIDENCE:
1) Location of bibliography files inspected:
   - repo/iclr2026_conference.bib (main .bib) contains many conference (inproceedings) entries. See file: [repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:1-300] and [repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:300-700].
   - repo/main.bbl (compiled bibliography) also lists the same references. See file: [repo/main.bbl:96-108] and [repo/main.bbl:200-216] for examples.

2) Examples of conference citations that include explicit proceedings links (these are verifiable within the repo because the .bib/.bbl contains a DOI or a direct URL to the official proceedings page):
   - Rajpurkar et al., "Know What You Don't Know" (ACL 2018) — repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:174-192 contains booktitle "Proceedings of the 56th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (...)" and explicit url/doi fields (url = https://aclanthology.org/P18-2124, doi = 10.18653/v1/P18-2124).
   - Rajpurkar et al., "SQuAD" (EMNLP 2016) — repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:194-214 contains booktitle "Proceedings of the 2016 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing" and url/doi (url = https://aclanthology.org/D16-1264, doi = 10.18653/v1/D16-1264).
   - Yang et al., "HotpotQA" (EMNLP 2018) — repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:303-312 includes doi = 10.18653/v1/D18-1259 (booktitle indicates EMNLP 2018 proceedings).
   - Manakul et al., "SelfCheckGPT" (EMNLP 2023) — repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:365-379 includes url = https://aclanthology.org/2023.emnlp-main.557/ and doi = 10.18653/v1/2023.emnlp-main.557.
   - Lin & Och, "Automatic Evaluation..." (ACL 2004) — repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:418-427 includes url = https://aclanthology.org/P04-1077/ and doi = 10.3115/1218955.1219032; the same appears in repo/main.bbl: [repo/main.bbl:181-186].
   - Orgad et al., ICLR 2025 — repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:323-329 includes url = https://openreview.net/forum?id=KRnsX5Em3W (OpenReview is the official ICLR reviewing/proceedings platform for those years).

   These in-repo DOI/URL fields are direct, verifiable pointers to the official proceedings pages and therefore are evidence that those specific citations point to proceedings entries.

3) Examples of conference citations that do NOT include a DOI or a proceedings URL in the .bib/.bbl (so their presence in the official proceedings cannot be confirmed from the repo alone):
   - han2024semantic ("Semantic Entropy Probes: ...") — repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:216-221 declares booktitle = "ICML 2024 Workshop on Foundation Models in the Wild" but contains no url or doi in the .bib.
   - he2021deberta (DeBERTa, ICLR 2021) — repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:233-238 lists booktitle = "International Conference on Learning Representations" and year = 2021 but no url/doi.
   - he2021debertav3 — repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:240-245 similarly lacks url/doi.
   - kuhn2023semantic (ICLR 2023) — repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:134-139 has booktitle = "The Eleventh International Conference on Learning Representations" and year = 2023 but no url/doi.
   - hansemantic (NeurIPS 2024 workshop) — repo/iclr2026_conference.bib:315-318 (also appears in repo/main.bbl: [repo/main.bbl:100-104]) shows the workshop/booktitle but no url/doi in the .bib.

4) Summary of automated presence scan (produced during analysis by parsing the .bib): some inproceedings entries have doi/url fields (thus verifiable from repo); others do not. The list of keys and whether they include a doi or url (computed while examining the .bib) includes both True and False cases — the False cases are the ones requiring external verification.

What additional information is needed to reach a conclusive PASS or FAIL:
 - Network access from this environment to the web (HTTP GET) so I can follow the conference proceedings URLs / search the official proceedings pages (publisher sites, ACL Anthology, OpenReview, NeurIPS proceedings) and check that each cited paper actually appears in the proceedings for the stated year. If web access is enabled I will fetch each proceedings page with a User-Agent header and confirm presence (or absence) and then return PASS if all are present, or FAIL if any cited paper is absent from the stated proceedings.
 - Alternatively, for each of the .bib entries that lack url/doi, provide the official proceedings page URL (or DOI) for the cited conference-year or the proceedings' table-of-contents listing, so I can verify presence without performing web searches.

Because some citations are verifiable from the repository (they include DOI/URL) while others are not, and because absence of an in-repo URL/DOI is not proof that the paper is missing from the proceedings, I cannot confidently mark the overall test PASS or FAIL based solely on repository contents. Therefore the correct overall verdict is INCONCLUSIVE.
