  - Hamilton (1834) DOI present: [/repo/iclr2025_conference.bbl:85-90] and in the .bib [/repo/iclr2025_conference.bib:67-75].
  - Watkins & Dayan (1992) DOI present: [/repo/iclr2025_conference.bbl:179-183] and in the .bib [/repo/iclr2025_conference.bib:85-93].
  - Greydanus & Olah (2019) DOI present: [/repo/iclr2025_conference.bbl:70-75] and in the .bib [/repo/iclr2025_conference.bib:102-109].
  - Mnih et al. (2015) DOI present: [/repo/iclr2025_conference.bbl:129-135] and in the .bib [/repo/iclr2025_conference.bib:129-136].
  - Bahri et al. (2020) DOI present: [/repo/iclr2025_conference.bbl:13-19] and in the .bib [/repo/iclr2025_conference.bib:188-196].
  - Hinton (2025) DOI present: [/repo/iclr2025_conference.bbl:91-96] and in the .bib [/repo/iclr2025_conference.bib:216-229].

- I ran an automated check (requests with an explicit User-Agent) and saved the results to an artifact you can inspect: /evidence/artifacts/doi_results.json. That file contains, for each DOI found in the main .bib/.bbl, the DOI request URL, the final redirected URL, HTTP status code, and extracted page title and citation meta tags (when present).
  - Location of the saved output: [/evidence/artifacts/doi_results.json]

- Summary of the HTTP-check results (from /evidence/artifacts/doi_results.json):
  - Successfully retrieved page metadata and matched titles/authors (examples):
    - 10.1007/BF00992698 -> final URL https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00992698; status 200; meta_title="Q-learning"; meta_authors include "Watkins, Christopher J. C. H." and "Dayan, Peter". (See artifact)
    - 10.23915/distill.00020 -> final URL https://distill.pub/2019/paths-perspective-on-value-learning/; status 200; meta_title and meta_authors present and matching the .bib entry.
    - 10.1038/nature14236 -> final URL https://www.nature.com/articles/nature14236; status 200; meta_title and meta_authors present and matching the .bib entry.
    - 10.1146/annurev-conmatphys-031119-050745 -> final URL https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/10.1146/annurev-conmatphys-031119-050745; status 200; meta_title and meta_authors present and matching the .bib entry.
  - Could NOT retrieve page metadata required for verification (blocked/JS redirect pages):
    - 10.1016/S0019-9958(58)80003-0 -> final URL https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0019995858800030; status 200 but page content contained "Redirecting" and no usable meta tags (likely requires JS or cookies).
    - 10.7551/mitpress/1535.003.0018 -> final URL https://direct.mit.edu/books/book/2884/chapter/78240/Optimal-Control-Theory; status 403 with a "Just a moment..." page (Cloudflare challenge), no meta tags available.
    - 10.1098/rstl.1834.0017 -> final URL https://royalsocietypublishing.org/...XV-On-a-general-method...; status 403 with "Just a moment..." page, no meta tags available.
    - 10.1103/RevModPhys.97.030502 -> final URL https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/RevModPhys.97.030502; status 403 with "Just a moment..." page, no meta tags available.

Why this is INCONCLUSIVE and what is needed to conclude PASS/FAIL:
- For the DOIs listed under "Could NOT retrieve page metadata", the DOI resolution did redirect to plausible publisher landing URLs but the landing pages returned bot-protection or JavaScript-interstitial pages, preventing automated extraction of title/author metadata via plain HTTP requests. Because the test requires confirming the landing page matches the cited title and authors, and I cannot extract those fields for these DOIs with the request method used, I cannot conclusively PASS or FAIL.

To make the check conclusive, one of the following additional steps is needed:
1) Allow the verifier to use a headless browser that executes JavaScript (e.g., Selenium / Playwright) so the Cloudflare/JS interstitials can be bypassed and the actual landing page HTML can be inspected for <title> and citation meta tags; or
2) Provide access to the landing-page HTML (or a human-accessed screenshot) for each blocked DOI so we can confirm the title/authors; or
3) Allow the use of a richer set of request headers/cookies or an interactive session that can pass any publisher bot checks (if permissible).

If you want, I can re-run the checks using a headless browser (Selenium) to try to collect the missing metadata and complete the verification. Otherwise, with the current HTTP-only approach the result is INCONCLUSIVE because several publisher landing pages are not machine-accessible in this environment.
